student_results_long: Expected data format for ReportR analysis functions

Source: R/student_results_long.R
student_results_long.Rd

All ReportR analysis functions expect a long-format data frame produced by standardize_student_results(). This page documents the required columns and their expected types.

Format

A data frame with one row per student per year per subject, with the following columns:

STUDENT_ID

character. Unique student identifier. Required for correlation analysis (run_correlations()).

YEAR

integer. Administration year. "YYYY_YYYY" academic-year strings are automatically converted to the end year by standardize_student_results().

GRADE

integer. Tested grade. NA for EOC subjects.

SUBJECT

character. Subject code matching keys in assessment_spec$subjects (e.g. "ELA", "MATHEMATICS").

SCALE_SCORE

numeric. Student scale score.

ACHIEVEMENT_LEVEL

character. Achievement level label matching assessment_spec$achievement_levels$labels.

SCHOOL_ID

character. School identifier.

SCHOOL_NAME

character. School name.

DISTRICT_ID

character. District identifier.

DISTRICT_NAME

character. District name.

RACE_ETHNICITY

character. Race/ethnicity category.

FRL

character. Free/reduced lunch status (binary demographic).

EL

character. English Learner status (binary demographic).

IEP

character. Individualized Education Program status (binary demographic).

GENDER

character. Student gender.

Details

Use standardize_student_results() to convert raw assessment data to this format. The function handles common variations in column naming (e.g. CONTENT_AREA -> SUBJECT, SS -> SCALE_SCORE) and coerces YEAR and GRADE to integer.

Important: Always call standardize_student_results() before filtering by year. Raw data from SGPdata uses "YYYY_YYYY" year strings; filtering by integer year before standardizing returns 0 rows.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
library(SGPdata)
library(dplyr)

student_results_long <- sgpData_LONG |>
  filter(VALID_CASE == "VALID_CASE") |>
  standardize_student_results()
} # }
